subject: AWS private offer: request for accelerated rev-share carveout + contract alignment
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer request — accelerated rev-share carveout / SLA ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — FastRetail is ready to move forward with a private AWS offer but procurement has two asks that require exception approval on your end:

1) Rev-share carveout for the first 3 months (customer-requested promotion) — they want a 30% carveout to pass through to a reseller.
2) Slight SLA relaxation for the private offer (99.5% for marketplace listing vs. your standard 99.9%) due to cross-region routing during rollout.

Procurement also asked for a 90-day revenue hold to cover onboarding refunds, and native net60 payment terms. I've attached our PO request with the procurement checklist.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate these exceptions or what approvals are required? Our procurement timeline is tight — they need a response by Friday 5/7.

Attachments: FastRetail_AWS_PO_Request.pdf (procurement checklist + requested terms)

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Director, Cloud Partnerships
FastRetail
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer request — accelerated rev-share carveout / SLA ask

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the PO. Looping in Legal (Marissa) and Marketplace Finance (Jonas) to scope the asks.

Quick take: the rev-share carveout and net60 are both things we can consider but they require executive signoff and a short financial model to show revenue impact. SLA relaxation to 99.5% is non-standard for private listings; Legal will need to review customer indemnity and fallback behavior.

I've attached a quick mutual action plan and a spreadsheet with the initial numbers I pulled together. Can you confirm: expected first-month consumption (tokens/embedding units) and who the reseller is (name + tax details)? That will help Jonas run the rev-share scenario.

Attachments: MA-FAST-4782.xlsx (mutual action plan + initial numbers)

Next steps:
- Jonas to send projected P&L impact by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa to review contract ask and highlight necessary redlines.
- I'll escalate to my leader for exec approval if needed.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer request — initial finance model

Karthik / Marissa — per Olivia's PO and the MA spreadsheet, I ran the three scenarios the customer asked about. See attached impact model (rev_share_impact_model.csv). Summary below:

- Baseline (no carveout): ARR impact +$720k over first 12 months.
- 30% Rev-share carveout (first 90 days): ARR decrease ~ -$110k (one-time impact normalized over year).
- 25% carveout (first 90 days) + $50k onboarding credit: ARR decrease ~ -$140k.

Notes / risks:
- Net60 pushes cash collection out, increasing working capital needs. Finance wants either an advance/shortened billing term for initial ramp or a revenue hold (they recommended 60–90 days depending on credit profile).
- SLA relaxation increases our expected incident exposure; legal should quantify indemnity delta.

Given the customer's timeline, the least dilutive path is: approve a 25% carveout for first 90 days, require a $50k onboarding credit (customer-funded or deducted from first invoice), and set revenue hold at 60 days (finance) — or 90 days if Legal or Sales request. That's the recommendation to minimize risk while staying competitive.

Attachments: revshare_impact_model.csv

- Jonas
Director, Marketplace Finance
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer request — contract redlines and legal flags

Karthik / Jonas — reviewed Olivia's requested terms. Legal flags the following non-standard items that require exec approval or modification:

1) Indemnity carveout requested by FastRetail for reseller pass-through — proposed language seeks broader indemnity than we accept. We can offer a limited reseller pass-through with capped liability and clear carveout for third-party reseller claims.
2) SLA change to 99.5%: acceptable only if coupled with explicit service credits and rollback/fallback to a hosted variant if regional routing fails.
3) Net60: we can accept net60 if Finance approves the revenue hold (60–90 days) and the customer signs a slightly longer commitment (12 months minimum).

I've prepared a redline with suggested counter-language and marked sections that will need exec signoff. Attaching redline for reference.

Attachments: redline_aws_po.docx

If Sales wants to proceed with the 25% carveout + $50k onboarding credit + 90-day hold, I can prepare a final redline for exec signature.

Marissa Cole
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Requesting exec approval — FastRetail private offer (DW-4782)

Vivek — we have a timeboxed procurement window with FastRetail. Summary and ask below:

Deal: FastRetail AWS private offer (deal_id: DW-4782-FAST)
Ask: Exec approval for non-standard commercial/contract terms to close this Q:
  • Rev-share carveout: approve up to 25% for first 90 days (customer wants 30%; finance/legal recommend 25%).
  • Onboarding credit: $50k (to be recouped from first invoice)
  • Revenue hold: 90 days (finance prefers 60 but Sales requests 90 to match customer ask)
  • SLA: allow 99.5% for the private listing with explicit service-credit schedule and fallback to hosted model if cross-region routing exceeds thresholds.
  • Net60 billing: accept if revenue hold and commitment (12 months) are in place.

Impact / rationale:
  • Competitive customer (FastRetail) with high ingress volume and a visible reseller channel; winning this will materially increase marketplace adoption and is strategically valuable.
  • Financial hit under the recommended package ~ -$140k ARR impact first year (Jonas' model).
  • Risk mitigations: 12-month commitment, onboarding credit recoup, revenue hold, capped indemnity (Marissa will provide redline).

Time sensitivity: procurement needs final position by EOD Friday 5/7 to keep AWS listing timing.

DocuSign link (prelim): https://docusign.com/FAST-PO/DW-4782
Attachments: MA-FAST-4782.xlsx, revshare_impact_model.csv, redline_aws_po.docx

Can you confirm approval (or any modifications) so we can respond to procurement?

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting exec approval — FastRetail private offer (DW-4782)

Karthik / team — thanks for the thorough analysis. Approve the following with the listed guardrails:

Approved items:
  • Rev-share carveout: up to 25% for the first 90 days only. No extension without a written business case and exec re-approval.
  • Onboarding credit: $50k approved but must be documented as a recoverable credit against the first invoice.
  • Revenue hold: 90 days as requested (Finance to manage collections and hold schedule).
  • SLA: allow 99.5% for listing but require service-credit schedule and automated fallback to hosted model; include clause for rollback if incident rate exceeds threshold for more than 14 days.
  • Net60: accept provided finance confirms billing setup and we have the 12-month minimum commitment signed.

Conditions:
  1) Legal to finalize redline with capped indemnity language and reseller pass-through limitation.
  2) Finance to confirm the revenue hold process and provide the billing schedule before countersign.
  3) Sales to secure written 12-month commitment and reseller tax details.

I've attached an exec memo for the record. Once Legal updates the redline we will route for exec signature. Good work team — please close the loop with Olivia and procurement.

Attachments: exec_approval_memo.pdf

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Marketplaces & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
